To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
galactitol (Dulcitol) dissimilation in Escherichica coli K12 is controlled by the following genetic loci: gatC, gatA, gatD, kba, fda, pfkA and pfkB-1.

the dissimilation pathway of galactitol in E. coli is via galactitol 1-P-D-tagotose-6-P and D-tagotose-1, 6-P2 to glycerol-3-P and D-fructose-6-P, that galactitol is transported via an enzyme II complex and a NAD dependent dehydogenase, that the gene locus kba codes for a ketose bis phosphate aldolase and that the genes pfkA
the dissimilation pathway of galactitol in E. coli is via galactitol-P-D-tagat-6-P-D-taga-1,6-bi-P, controlled by gatC A, D, pfk A, pfkB- 1 and kba.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic analysis of the dissimilation pathway of galactitol in E. coli.
the analysis of the dissimilation pathway of the sugar alcohols mannitol, sorbitol, dulcitol and xylitol.
the analysis of the dissimilation and the regulation of galactitol in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

galactitol dissimilatory metabolism in E. coli is via the following reaction sequence: galactitol+ATP↔galactitol-1-phosphate+ADP galactitol- 1-phosphate+D-6-phosphogluconolactone↔D-tagatose- 6-phosphate+D-lactone phosphate D-tagatose 6-phosphate↔D-tagotose 1,6-bis-phosphate D-tagatose

the dissimilation pathway of galactitol is via galactitol→galactitol-1-phosphate→D-tagatose-2-6-phosphate→D-fructose-1-6-phosphate, and that this pathway is controlled by at least six genetic loci: gatC A B D (gat operon), pfkA and kba.

galactitol dissimilatory enzymes of E. coli are controlled by the genetic locus gatC, the structural genes gtaA and gatB for the enzyme II-complex Gat and a soluble, inducible, NAD dependent galactitol-6-dehydrogenase, and that the galactitol pathway is branched by a temperature sensitive ketohexose-1, 6-bisphosphate aldolase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
galactitol dissimilatory mutants of E. coli are of two types.
the galactitol dissimilatory system in E. coli is made up of at least five genes and that the genes gatD, pfkA and kba are not linked.

the galactitol dissimilatory system in E. coli consists of three different genetic loci: gat for the transport and phosphorylation of galactitol and for the dehydrogenation of galactitol, pfk for the phosphorylation of D-tagatone-1,6-bis-phosphate and kba for the cleavage of D-tagatotne-1,6-diphosphate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dissimilation pathway of galactitol is a very complicated one and is affected by a number of genes.
we have identified the genes and the enzymes that are responsible for galactitol metabolism in E. coli and that these genes are located in a single operon.
we were able to identify and characterize a new gene locus, kba, which controls an enzyme, a ketose-bisphosphate aldolase, which is essential for galactitol dissimiliation in E. coli.
